query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A trace addition of boron (approximately 0.5 atomic percent) introduced during alloy processing will enhance the grain-boundary cohesion of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38, thereby significantly improving its load-bearing integrity without noticeably degrading its caloric (magnetocaloric and pressure-induced) performance.
generation.material_initial_state: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is polycrystalline with relatively coarse grains, exhibiting a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields but prone to cracking and exhibiting poor mechanical integrity under load.
generation.intervention: Incorporate approximately 0.5 atomic percent boron into the alloy during processing.
generation.conditions: The alloy is operated under applied magnetic and pressure fields near room temperature, within the thermal and loading regimes used for refrigeration applications where cracking has been observed.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron is expected to segregate to the grain boundaries forming boride or boron-rich precipitates that enhance grain-boundary cohesion and mitigate stress concentration sites.
generation.mechanism: By refining the intergranular chemistry, the boron addition reduces grain-boundary embrittlement and inhibits crack initiation and propagation. This intervention is designed to improve the load-bearing capability without altering the phase transformation mechanisms responsible for the magnetocaloric and pressure-induced caloric effects.
generation.predicted_outcome: The boron-doped alloy will exhibit significantly enhanced fracture toughness and reduced crack propagation under mechanical loads, while the magnitude of its caloric responses (temperature/entropy changes under applied fields) remains close to that of the undoped baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, characterized by high caloric performance but limited mechanical integrity (i.e., a tendency to crack under load).
generation.boundary: The expected improvements are anticipated under the same applied magnetic and pressure fields and within the operational temperature range, particularly during cyclic or sustained load conditions where cracking previously limited performance.
generation.uncertainty: The precise optimal boron concentration and any subtle effects on the kinetics of the caloric phase transformation are uncertain and require experimental calibration. It is also uncertain if boron addition might introduce any unexpected secondary phases that could affect the caloric response over long-term cycling.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples using identical processing parameters: one control group with the standard (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 composition and one experimental group with an additional 0.5 at% boron. Subject both sets to identical thermal, magnetic, and pressure cycles that mimic operation in refrigeration conditions. Evaluate mechanical integrity (using fracture toughness tests and fatigue cycling) and caloric response (by quantifying temperature and/or entropy changes under applied fields).
measurements: Fracture toughness (e.g., using standardized crack propagation tests)
Fatigue crack growth rates under cyclic loading
Caloric response metrics (e.g., magnetocaloric effect quantified by ΔT or ΔS and barocaloric effect under pressure cycling)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped alloy does not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in fracture toughness and fatigue resistance while retaining caloric performance within ±10% of the control samples, or if the boron addition causes a measurable degradation in the caloric effect, then the hypothesis is falsified.
